title: The Lean problem set
html:
The Lean problem set

The problems for the AI-model tests (see the Lean experiment design). Agents prove theorems in Lean 4.35.0, with Lean's core library and no Mathlib; Lean checks every proof, and a proof records exactly which earlier theorems it uses.

Public here: the definitions every agent sees (Problems/Defs.lean) and the posted targets (Problems/Targets.lean). Three areas: a number sequence (A), sorting (B) and 2 × 2 integer matrices (C), with targets that join areas.

Also public: the reference proofs (Reference/) and the lemma tree they give (reference-dag.md, reference-dag-hard.md), since 2026-11-09. Agents in a run are not given them. A model trained after that date may have seen them, so keep that in mind when choosing a new model for these problems.

Not in this repository: agents' transcripts, which are large (lean/runs/).

Target Area Statement Bounty
C3 C det(xy) = det(x)·det(y) 4
A3 A u(m) divides u(m·k) 8
C4 C x^(m·n) = (x^m)^n 16
X1 A + C Cassini: u(n+1)² − u(n+2)·u(n) = (−3)^n 16
B3 B insertion sort returns a sorted list with the same counts 32
B5 B merge sort and insertion sort agree 64
X2 A + B sorting u(0), …, u(n−1) leaves them unchanged 64
A5 A strong divisibility: gcd(u(m), u(n)) = u(gcd(m, n)) 256

Rules for agents: core lemmas and tactics may be cited freely (they play the role of existing literature). Not allowed: grind (it proves the polynomial identities by brute force and would flatten the tree), sorry, native_decide, search tactics, commands that run code, and new declarations.

The pilot (npm run pilot, in src/lean/) measures how hard each theorem is for a real model:

npm run pilot -- selftest                       # every reference proof through the checker
npm run pilot -- calibrate --dry-run            # how many attempts and calls a run makes
npm run pilot -- calibrate                      # the real run; needs an API key in .env
  • An attempt is a first proof plus up to three repairs, each sent back with Lean's errors. Each theorem is tried with its lemmas given as a library, and each target also alone, to test whether it really needs them.
  • The checker (src/lean/checker.ts) imports only the public definitions and states the agent's library as axioms. #print axioms then lists exactly which library theorems a proof used: the soundness check and the attribution in one. A check takes about 0.3 seconds. All 42 reference proofs pass, using exactly the theorems the reference tree says.
  • Transcripts are large, so they stay out of this repository (lean/runs/).
